name: Longitude 131
positioning: Luxury tented camp among the red dunes of Australia's Red Centre, with views to Uluru and Kata Tjuta and guided experiences included in the tariff
best_for: Travelers who want to explore Uluru and Kata Tjuta with guides, with the core experiences included
Couples and adult travelers seeking a design-led desert camp with Aboriginal art and culture woven in

facts.text: Longitude 131 has views direct to Uluru and across the desert to Kata Tjuta.
The lodge sits on privately owned land surrounded by Katiti Aboriginal Land and the dual World Heritage listed Uluru-Kata Tjuta National Park.
Guests stay in tented pavilions among the dunes, with floor-to-ceiling glass framing the desert light.
Longitude 131 first opened in 2002, with safari-style tents gathered around a central Dune House designed by Australian architect Philip Cox.
The lodge's sustainable design includes renewable energies and the ability to be dismantled and removed entirely.
Spa Kinara uses irmangka-irmangka, also known as Scented Emu Bush, a bush medicine used by Aboriginal healers, in many treatments.
Signature experiences include a guided sunrise expedition to Kata Tjuta and Walpa Gorge.
Artist Bruce Munro's Field of Light installation is one of the signature experiences.
Scenic helicopter flights lift off from the lodge's helipad, at additional charge.
Dining combines premium produce from around Australia with bush ingredients.
The in-tent bar is included in the stay.

highlights.text: Each luxury tent offers views to Uluru from the end of the bed.
The Dune Top has a help-yourself bar, outdoor lounges and a plunge spa with views to both Uluru and Kata Tjuta.
Signature experiences are included in the tariff and run on a shared basis with fellow guests at scheduled times.
Spa Kinara is inspired by the design of the wiltja, the traditional shelter of the local Anangu people.
The lodge hosts artists-in-residence visits with Ernabella Arts, where guests can watch Anangu artists paint with views of Uluru and Kata Tjuta.

considerations.text: Longitude 131 welcomes children ten years and over.
The gateway is Ayers Rock Airport, three hours by air from most Australian capital cities.
Conde Nast Traveler notes the pool is a bit petite.
